proof.surface: A real nats-server v2.11.4, a real envoy-listener built from this head (go build ./cmd/listener), and a fake agent session subscribed to notifications.slack.> that receives Slack deliveries over prompt_async, which is the path Deliverer.Text writes. The rig posts a signed Slack bot_message to the listener's /webhook/slack address.

The same rig run against the parent commit's listener (the plan's 'What goes wrong today' measurement) gave 'Summary: slack bot message in C_RIG from datadog: ' and a payload with no text field at all.

trickyParts: A section block carries its words in a nested object (text: {type: mrkdwn, text: ...}), so the walk takes the strings under the seven display field names and then descends, in sorted key order, into every value of the object that is not a string. Without that second pass a block's words never reach the output.
Seeding the walk with the message's own text goes through the same take() as every other piece, so the rune count that decides the cut counts the own text too.
The committed claude-envoy plugin bundle mirrors skills/, and the required 'Check the committed bundle is fresh' CI step (bun run check-dist) fails if the skill file is edited without rebuilding it.

Three of the plan's test cases that it expected to fail before the change are guards instead, because the architect's containment rule made their expectation today's behaviour: a_repeated_piece, own_words_and_a_rich-text_block and a_contained_piece_shorter_than_the_words. Together with the plan's own three guards (the file-only message, the deleted message, and the two 'shapes that carry nothing' cases whose payload stays empty) that is the 7 of 18 cases that pass at the parent commit.
deviations: The repeat check is containment, not whole equality: a piece is not taken when the text collected so far already contains it as a substring. This is the architect's decision of 2026-10-25T03:14:47Z (Envoy message 2283f04bcf184186ab5c6990da702222 to notifications.role.legion-infra-infra-180-implementer), which it gave as this round's authority, because a message composed in a Slack client carries a rich_text copy of its own words split per segment and whole equality would deliver 'Deploy failed <@U1>' followed by 'Deploy failed '. Everything else in the approved rule is unchanged. Two cases the architect named are in the table: a_contained_piece_shorter_than_the_words (own text 'deploy to web-1 failed' with an attachment value 'web-1' delivers the own text alone) and a_piece_that_extends_one_already_taken (fallback 'CPU high' then a block 'CPU high on host-a' delivers both lines).

The three departures the plan recorded stand as the architect accepted them: the order inside one object is Slack's display order (Go's decoded map keeps no key order), the guard cases cannot fail before the change, and T4 edits skills/legion-controller/references/slack-mentions.md as well as the changelog. The regenerated claude-envoy bundle copy of that skill file is the one file beyond T4's two, and it is generated rather than written.

Two of the six findings of the ce-simplify-code pass were applied, at head e587427d7f0c, giving the new head 4ea17e805b03: the walk collects the keys it will descend into before sorting them (a block leaf whose values are all strings now sorts and allocates nothing), and the collected rune count grows with the text instead of being recounted on every piece. Both are byte-identical in output; the repository's checks and the rig proof above were re-run on the applied head. The four skipped: the reuse reviewer's removal of the string filter (superseded by the efficiency fix, which keeps the filter and moves it before the sort), the quality reviewer's removal of the test table's wantNoText field (the flag names the asserted condition at each case, which is what a table test is for), its rename and move of the integration test (the plan names that test and that file), and its slackView struct (a wider refactor than this diff, and the plan settled the two signatures).
discoveredComplexity: Acceptance 2's lane cannot run on an issue pod: packages/envoy/internal/integration starts a real NATS server through testcontainers and this pod has neither Docker nor Podman. The test is compiled and type-checked here (go vet ./internal/integration/ and go test -run NoSuchTest ./internal/integration/ both clean) and runs in CI, in the envoy-go job of 'Legion Envoy and Contracts' (go test ./internal/integration/ -timeout 300s -count=1), run 40161054391 on this head. It is a regression lock, not the proof of the symptom, which the rig carries.

The rig is a throwaway at packages/envoy/out/e2e/infra180-slack-wake-rig.sh, an ignored path, so nothing of it is committed; its text is in the plan document (dispatch://INFRA-180/artifact/plan-md, 'The live rig'), and its prerequisites on a pod are go, bun, jq, openssl, curl and a nats-server binary from GOBIN=<dir> go install github.com/nats-io/nats-server/v2@v2.11.4.
